text: @CC @rcalo @EdFelten44 FYI, some reflections on the AI workshops above.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 17. So, in short, good turn of events but I want to emphasize that this is not a panacea from either an AI policy or democratic perspective.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 16. What is *done* with this report after it's produced will also be critical, and again, this is not immune from biases/constraints/etc.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 15. So, as in a lot of things sci./tech policy-related, processes are key - and beyond the livestreaming, there is ~ no accountability here.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 14. Among other potential biases here are those for low/no regulation, and with many corporations involved here, advisory capture is a risk.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 13. This is not intrinsically bad - some of those biases may be good, and science being political isn't unheard of - but it should be known.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 12. It will reflect not just what happens at the workshops but various political constraints/biases of those involved at and around OSTP.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 11. it is also clear that as in similar cases (see, e.g. Krimsky's Genetic Alchemy on Asilomar) this will hardly be an apolitical document.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 10. One final area of caveating/mild critique regards the report to be produced after the workshops. This could be a great report, but...

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 9. or the National Citizens' Technology Forum: https://t.co/LXFewUPbsX That sort of thing may follow the workshops but they're not the same.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 8. For examples of serious efforts at engagement, see e.g. https://t.co/skGdN9ttJl (asteroids, in which I participated as a facilitator), ..

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 7. And even if all were interested in it, not all could go. This is why robust such efforts do things like compensate people for their time.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 6. Among many other reasons why this isn't on the cutting edge of such things, self-selection will play a huge role in participation.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 5. It will have lots of value, IMO, but to actually engage the public on AI, one would need to look at and learn from prior similar efforts.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 4. Now on to some mild critiques/caveats - it would be a mistake to accept the framing of this as a real public engagement effort. It's not.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 3. Last point of praise: the task force on AI for government is much needed. U.S. Digital Service, etc. are good but AI seems underutilized.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: 2. Also, the thematic grouping of the workshops makes sense as does livestreaming them, and they seem to have good speakers lined up so far.
